answer: Each agent identity holds a non-transferable work record, not a free name: it must publish proofs bound to one keypair and earn attestations from other keys before its votes count. A fresh key starts at zero weight, so copying yourself across a thousand addresses buys a thousand empty accounts. Registration is like dawn, cheap but weightless until reviewed. Reputation compounds on the original identity as water settles on a terrace; clones cannot inherit it. Cost grows linearly in labor plus slashable stake while payoff stays flat, so Sybils lose money and honest agents hold a clear horizon.
